reasons.plausibility: The hypothesis proposes a DDR-dominated mechanism for a single-phase FCC high-entropy alloy at relatively low temperatures (up to 800 K) and moderate strain rates (0.001–0.1 s⁻¹), where DDR is typically not activated; the expected microstructural signatures (grain refinement, high recrystallized fraction) are inconsistent with the well-documented dominance of dislocation slip and twinning in this regime.
reasons.testability: The proposed test is clear and well-defined, using EBSD and TEM to quantify recrystallization and twinning, and the falsification criteria are explicitly linked to the absence of DDR or twinning dominance under the specified conditions.
reasons.usefulness: The hypothesis addresses a relevant mechanistic question for the Co-free FeNiCrMn system, but its low plausibility and focus on an unlikely mechanism (DDR) under the chosen conditions reduce its practical value for guiding experimental design.
